title: They Fell Out of Love… or They Starved for Appreciation?
paragraphs: They Fell Out of Love… or They Starved for Appreciation?
Why the words you stopped saying slowly killed what romance could never save
It didn’t end with shouting.
It didn’t collapse in betrayal.
It died quietly… in the spaces where “thank you” should have lived.
There are relationships that don’t break because love disappears… they break because appreciation does.
And somewhere deep inside you, you already know that’s true.
Because you remember the beginning.

You remember the way even the smallest things felt seen. The way a simple message, a gentle look, a quiet “I appreciate you” felt like oxygen to your soul. You didn’t need grand gestures. You didn’t need perfect romance. You just needed to feel valued.
But then life happened.
Familiarity replaced wonder. Assumptions replaced gratitude. Presence replaced pursuit.
And suddenly… the person you once celebrated became someone you silently expected.
That’s where love begins to starve.
Scripture never said love survives on romance.
It said something deeper… something uncomfortable… something we often ignore.

In the original Greek, when Paul writes in 1 Thessalonians 5:18, he uses the word “εὐχαριστεῖτε” (eucharisteite) — meaning to give thanks, to express gratitude intentionally, continuously, not based on feeling but on obedience.
“In everything give thanks…” wasn’t poetry.
It was instruction.
Because God knows something we often learn too late…
Appreciation sustains what romance can only ignite.
Romance excites the heart.
Appreciation anchors it.
Romance says, “I feel something for you.”
Appreciation says, “I see you.”
And people don’t leave where they feel seen.
But let’s go deeper… because this isn’t just about relationships.
This is about how we treat God Himself.
In Luke 17, ten lepers were healed.
Ten.
But only one came back.
Only one returned to say thank you.
Jesus responds with words that still echo today:
“οὐχὶ οἱ δέκα ἐκαθαρίσθησαν; οἱ δὲ ἐννέα ποῦ;”
“Were not all ten cleansed? Where are the nine?”
Where are the nine…
That question is heavier than it sounds.
Because it reveals something terrifying.
Miracles don’t guarantee gratitude.
Blessings don’t guarantee appreciation.
And a heart that stops appreciating… eventually stops loving rightly.
Maybe that’s what happened to you.
Or maybe… that’s what’s happening through you.
You didn’t mean to become ungrateful.
You just got used to what you once prayed for.
And that’s how appreciation dies.
Not through rebellion… but through neglect.
Even in Hebrew thought, gratitude isn’t passive.
The word “יָדָה” (yadah) means to give thanks with extended hands — a posture of surrender, recognition, acknowledgment.
Gratitude was never meant to be silent.
It was meant to be expressed.
Felt.
Given.
Shared.
Because unspoken appreciation slowly turns into invisible love.
And invisible love… eventually feels like no love at all.
This is why some of you are exhausted.
Not because love is gone…
But because appreciation is absent.
You’ve been giving… without being acknowledged.
Showing up… without being seen.
Serving… without being valued.
And it’s draining something deep inside you.
But here’s the truth that might change everything…
Jesus never built His relationship with us on romance.
He built it on sacrificial appreciation.
He saw us at our worst… and still chose us.
He valued us when we were broken.
He pursued us when we were undeserving.
Romans 5:8 doesn’t sound romantic.
It sounds real.
“But God demonstrates His love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
That word “demonstrates” comes from the Greek “συνίστησιν” (synistēsin) — meaning to prove, to establish, to show by action.
Not by feeling.
Not by words alone.
But by evidence.
Jesus didn’t just say He loved you.
He showed you your worth.
That’s appreciation at its highest form.
And if we’re honest…
We crave that kind of love more than romance.
We crave to be known.
To be valued.
To be remembered in the small things.
To be appreciated without having to beg for it.
So let me ask you something you might not be ready to answer…
When was the last time you truly appreciated the people God placed in your life?
Not assumed them.
Not expected from them.
But genuinely… intentionally… appreciated them?
Because if you wait until they’re gone…
Your gratitude becomes grief.
And grief always says what appreciation should have said earlier.
This isn’t just about fixing relationships.
This is about repentance.
Because ingratitude isn’t just relational…
It’s spiritual.
In Romans 1:21, Paul exposes something chilling:
“Because, although they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God, nor were thankful…”
Not thankful.
That was the beginning of their fall.
Not immorality.
Not rebellion.
Ingratitude.
A heart that stops appreciating God… will eventually drift from God.
And a heart that stops appreciating people… will eventually lose them.
So maybe this message isn’t here to entertain you.
Maybe it’s here to interrupt you.
To wake something up.
To remind you that appreciation is not optional in love…
It is essential.
And maybe right now, there’s a name coming to your mind.
Someone you’ve overlooked.
Someone you’ve taken for granted.
Someone who stayed… when they didn’t have to.
Don’t ignore that.
That’s conviction.
That’s God knocking.
Don’t wait.
Reach out.
Say what you’ve been withholding.
Restore what silence has been breaking.
Because appreciation has the power to resurrect what romance could never revive.
And if this touched something deep in you…
Be honest.
Let people see they’re not alone in this.
Your honesty might be the permission someone else needs to heal.
Don’t assume they know.
Say it.
And if you feel something different right now… something deeper than emotion… something that feels like conviction mixed with hope…
Stay close.
Because this is not just content.
This is discipleship.
And for those who are serious about going deeper…
And if this ministry is feeding your spirit…
Support it.
Not out of pressure… but out of purpose.
Because when you invest in what glorifies God… you become part of the mission.
Because following Jesus was never meant to be passive.
It was meant to be lived.
Felt.
Shared.
Multiplied.
And maybe the love you’ve been looking for…
Was never missing.
It was just waiting to be appreciated.
